metaDescription: Six electric griddles compared on cooking surface, temperature range, grease control and cleanup, from compact flat tops to 22-inch family-size plates.
introParagraphs: An electric griddle turns a counter into a flat top for pancakes, eggs, bacon and sandwiches, with no burner to tend and no pan to balance. The best ones heat evenly, hold a steady temperature, and clean up without a fight. Size is the first decision, because a 22-inch plate and a 15-inch plate are different appliances.

The second decision is how the griddle handles the practical side of cooking. A removable temperature probe, a drip tray, cool-touch edges and detachable handles all change how safe and storable the unit is. This lineup runs from the 10 by 20 inch Chefman XL to the 22-inch Presto and Gourmia plates and the 20-inch Dash. We evaluated six models based on product specs and buyer feedback.

Use the decision tables to match surface area, control style and storage to your kitchen. Whatever you pick, plan a level counter, keep the cord out of walkways, and let the plate cool completely before washing it so the surface does not warp.

products.name: Chefman XL Electric Griddle, Removable Control
products.description:
The Chefman XL gives you a 10 by 20 inch nonstick plate and a 200 to 420F temperature range, which covers everything from keeping food warm to a hard sear. The temperature control detaches, and with it removed the body can be immersed for washing. A drip tray collects excess oil and grease so the plate stays cleaner during cooking.

The removable control is both a strength and a rule. The probe must stay out of the water, and it has to be attached before each use, which is one more step to remember. There is no tilt design for draining fat, so grease depends on the drip tray rather than gravity.

Compared with the compact Chefman, the XL doubles the useful width for batches, and compared with the 22-inch Presto 07061, it is a narrower but easier-to-store shape. It is the best all-round choice for a household that wants a big plate without a banquet-size footprint. In daily use, the routine is short: seat the probe, preheat, cook, let the plate cool, then detach the probe before washing. The drip tray should be emptied once it is cool, so grease never ends up on the counter or in the cord area.
products.bestFor: Families who want a roomy plate that is easy to wash.

products.name: Presto 07061 22-Inch Electric Ceramic Griddle
products.description:
Presto's 07061 offers a 22-inch cooking surface with a PFAS-free ceramic coating and a textured nonstick finish. It is the roomiest plate here for feeding a table at once. Detachable handles let the unit fit into most standard 18-inch cabinets.

The handles must be attached before each use, which is a small chore and a small safety step. Ceramic needs nylon or wooden utensils, so metal spatulas are out. There is no tilt feature to drain fat, so greasy foods rely on the plate's design instead.

Against the Presto 07047 at 10.5 by 16 inches, this model trades footprint for capacity, and against the Gourmia at 22 inches it is closer in size but differs in its handle and surface details. Choose it if you regularly cook for four or more and want storage that still fits a standard cabinet. Remember to clip the handles on before you heat the unit, and let the plate cool completely before taking them off again. Wipe the textured surface with a soft sponge so food residue does not collect in the pattern.
products.bestFor: Large households that cook for crowds on a regular basis.

products.name: Presto 07047 16-Inch Cool Touch Electric Griddle
products.description:
This Presto has a mid-size 10.5 by 16 inch plate, a cool-touch base along the front and sides, and a built-in backstop ledge. Those details make it the most reassuring griddle to handle. The cooking surface is a PFAS-free ceramic nonstick, which keeps cleanup simple.

The tradeoffs are modest. There is no tilt feature to drain grease, and it needs more storage room than a very compact unit. Ceramic coatings call for nylon or wood tools. The plate itself still gets hot, even though the base stays cooler.

Compared with the Chefman XL's 10 by 20 inch plate, the Presto 07047 is shorter but adds the cool-touch base and ledge. Compared with the Presto 07061, it gives up a lot of area for a more manageable size. It suits one to three people who value safer handling. Because the edges stay cooler than the plate, reaching past it to grab a plate or a pan is less risky, though you should still treat the whole unit as hot. Storage is easy enough on a pantry shelf, as long as the cord is wrapped loosely and the plate is dry.

products.name: Dash Deluxe Everyday Electric Griddle, 20-Inch
products.description:
The Dash Deluxe is a 20-inch family-size griddle with a 1500W heating element that reaches cooking temperature quickly. What sets it apart is the plate: both the nonstick cooking plate and the drip tray pop off, and they can be hand washed or put straight in the dishwasher. Many griddles use a fixed cooktop.

Speed and cleanup are the highlights, and the tradeoffs are that more removable parts mean more places for grease to creep during use. A detachable plate also needs to be seated properly each time. Its listing does not state a temperature range here, so confirm the dial settings in the manual.

Against the Chefman XL, the Dash gives you an easier plate wash but not an immersible body. Against the Amazon Basics griddle, it shares the removable plate idea but offers a larger size. It is the cleanup pick for people who dread scrubbing a fixed plate. After cooking, let the plate cool, lift it off, and rinse or load it. The fast heat-up also helps on school mornings, when waiting for a cold plate to warm slows everything down.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Griddle, Ceramic Coating
products.description:
The Amazon Basics griddle has a ceramic nonstick coating, a temperature range of 200 to 400F set by a removable probe, and a detachable plate that is dishwasher safe. Deep channels guide run-off grease into a removable drip tray. It is a straightforward design with the cleanup features that matter most.

A 400F ceiling is slightly lower than the Chefman's 420F, which matters only if you want very hard sears. The probe must be attached before cooking, so there is a small setup step. The listing in the brief does not state the plate dimensions, so check the size before you buy.

Compared with the Dash Deluxe, it also has a removable plate but without the 1500W claim. Compared with the Gourmia, it offers a similar 200 to 400F range. Choose it if you want sensible features without extras. Day to day, the main habit is to wipe the plate while it is warm but not hot, then let the detached plate air dry. The tray should be emptied after each use, which keeps the channels from clogging with old grease.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want dishwasher-safe parts and clear grease channels.

products.name: Gourmia Electric Griddle, 22-Inch XL Ceramic
products.description:
The Gourmia is a 22-inch griddle with a nonstick ceramic flat top and adjustable temperature control from 200 to 400 degrees. A pull-out drip tray handles grease, and the listing stresses easy cleanup. The plate size matches the Presto 07061, which makes it a serious option for families.

On the downside, the stated top temperature is 400F, a little below the Chefman. It is a large appliance, so counter and cabinet space are real requirements. Ceramic coatings reward gentle utensils.

Compared with the Presto 07061, the Gourmia advertises precise temperature control and a pull-out tray rather than detachable handles. Compared with the Dash Deluxe at 20 inches, it adds two inches of cooking area. Pick it if you want maximum space and straightforward controls. The pull-out tray makes the end of a meal easier, though you should wait for the plate to cool before sliding it out. Plan a permanent counter spot or a low shelf, because lifting a 22-inch appliance repeatedly is not ideal for everyone.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Surface area decides how many pancakes or eggs cook at once, and a larger plate needs more counter and storage space. The Chefman XL offers 10 by 20 inches, the Dash Deluxe 20 inches, and the Presto 07061 and Gourmia both 22 inches. For one or two people, 10.5 by 16 inches on the Presto 07047 is plenty. Measure your counter before choosing a 22-inch model.

A wide range lets you warm food at the low end and sear at the high end. The Chefman lists 200 to 420F while the Amazon Basics and Gourmia list 200 to 400F. Pancakes and eggs use the middle of the range, so the difference rarely matters for breakfast. It matters only if you sear burgers often.

A removable probe allows immersion washing in some models, but the probe itself must stay dry. The Chefman XL and Amazon Basics both use a removable control. Attach it fully before each use and confirm the light or click if there is one. If you prefer a fixed dial, check that the listing says so.

A drip tray or channel steers grease away from food. The Chefman XL, Amazon Basics and Gourmia all use a drip tray, and the Dash has a pop-off tray. Tilt designs help drain fat more, but none of the six here use a tilt. Empty the tray after the plate cools to avoid spills.

Cool-touch bases keep the housing cooler than the cooking surface, but the plate itself still gets hot. The Presto 07047 adds a cool-touch base and a backstop ledge. Treat every edge as warm and keep pets and children away. A ledge also helps with flipping.

Ceramic coatings need nylon or wooden tools and no metal scrapers. Let the plate cool before washing to avoid warping. The Amazon Basics and Dash offer dishwasher-safe plates, which are the easiest to maintain. Fixed plates need careful hand washing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Plate size and shape
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated surface dimensions against how many servings they can feed. The Presto 07061 and Gourmia at 22 inches lead on capacity, with the Dash at 20 inches and Chefman XL at 10 by 20 inches next. The Presto 07047 earns credit for a manageable size.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat control
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed temperature ranges and control style. The Chefman XL reaches 420F, while the Amazon Basics and Gourmia stop at 400F. Removable probes earned credit for washing flexibility but a small penalty for the extra step.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at cool-touch edges, backstop ledges and stable handles. The Presto 07047 leads on cool-touch design and ledge. Detachable handles on the Presto 07061 improve storage but add a step.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleanup and grease
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed drip trays, removable plates and dishwasher claims. The Dash Deluxe and Amazon Basics earned top marks for removable plates. Fixed-plate designs need more care to keep clean.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the feature set
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each model to a household type. The Chefman XL is the balanced all-rounder, the Presto 07061 and Gourmia the big-batch picks, the Presto 07047 the safety-minded pick, and the Dash and Amazon Basics the cleanup picks.

faq.q: Which electric griddle should I buy?
faq.a: The Chefman XL is the best overall because its 10 by 20 inch plate and immersible body balance size and cleanup. For crowds, the Presto 07061 and Gourmia both offer 22 inches. For safer handling, the Presto 07047 adds a cool-touch base and ledge.

faq.q: What temperature should I use for pancakes?
faq.a: Most cooks use the middle of the range, which on these griddles falls around the 350F area. Preheat until the indicator shows ready, and adjust after the first batch. Eggs prefer a lower setting than burgers. If the first pancake browns too fast, drop the dial a notch rather than moving the batter, since the plate holds heat well after it is up to temperature. Wipe the plate lightly between batches.

faq.q: Can I wash an electric griddle in water?
faq.a: Only when the temperature control is removed. The Chefman XL and Amazon Basics both use removable probes, and the probe must stay dry. The Dash Deluxe plate and tray can go in the dishwasher, but check each manual first.

faq.q: Do ceramic plates need special care?
faq.a: Yes. Use nylon or wooden utensils, avoid metal scrapers, and let the plate cool before washing. Gentle care keeps the nonstick surface working longer and prevents warping. A little oil is still useful for foods that stick, and a soft cloth removes residue better than abrasive pads.

faq.q: Does a bigger griddle cook faster?
faq.a: It cooks more at once, not faster per piece. A 22-inch plate like the Presto 07061 saves time on big batches. For one or two people, a smaller plate heats up sooner and uses less counter space.

faq.q: Are cool-touch griddles safe to touch?
faq.a: Only the base is cooler. The cooking surface on the Presto 07047 is still hot. Treat the whole unit as warm and keep hands on handles. Keep children and pets away from the cord, and never place a hot plate on a cold, wet surface because the temperature shock can damage the coating.

faq.q: How do I store a large griddle?
faq.a: Removable handles help. The Presto 07061 fits most standard 18-inch cabinets once the handles are off. Measure your cabinet before buying any 20 or 22-inch model.
